*Early Life and Accession*
Raymond III was born around 1140 to Raymond II Count of Tripoli and Hodierna of Jerusalem. His father was assassinated in 1152 leaving the young boy as count. He ruled under the regency of his mother and later under King Baldwin III of Jerusalem. He received homage from the nobles of Tripoli and secured his position.

*Rule as Count of Tripoli*
Raymond III married Eschiva of Bures Princess of Galilee gaining control of Galilee and Tiberias. He balanced his loyalties between the Kingdom of Jerusalem and the County of Tripoli. He participated in diplomatic missions to negotiate with Nur ad Din and later with Saladin. He defended Tripoli against Muslim raids and maintained the fortifications. He also intervened in the succession disputes of Jerusalem supporting the claim of Isabella I.

*Relations with the Kingdom of Jerusalem*
Raymond III sometimes allied with the royal faction and at other times opposed it. He backed the candidacy of Baldwin IV during his minority. He later grew disillusioned with the rule of Guy of Lusignan and withdrew his support. His shifting stance contributed to the factionalism that weakened the Crusader states before the Battle of Hattin.

*Later Years and Death*
In his final years Raymond III retired from active politics and focused on the administration of his counties. He died in 1187 shortly before the decisive defeat at Hattin. His death left the County of Tripoli to his son Raymond IV who continued to resist Muslim advances until the fall of the city in 1289.
